empty.title: Make your first Bot
empty.body: A Bot is an assistant that lives on one of your computers: it takes on tasks and asks you before risky steps.
empty.reach: Talk to it here, in {{telegram}}, {{slack}} or {{discord}}, or from any app, agent or program that speaks HTTP, including OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP clients.

list.noComputer.body: Get a computer first, then come back to make your first Bot.
list.noRunning.title: None of your computers is running
list.noRunning.body: A Bot runs on a running computer. Start one to see its Bots and make new ones.
list.noMatchStopped: {{name}} is stopped, so there are no Bots to list
filter.computer.unknown: A computer not on this realm

notice.otherRealm: This computer serves another realm. Switch realm to see its Bots.
notice.starting: Starting. Its Bots show here when it runs.
notice.more: More Bots than the list can show.
notice.paused_one: {{count}} Bot is paused after a sign-in change.
notice.paused_other: {{count}} Bots are paused after a sign-in change.

detail.none.title: Select a Bot
detail.none.body: Its page shows what it is doing, what needs you, its link and keys, its settings and its chat apps. A Bot lives on one computer and, with permission, can use the other computers of its realm.
bot.aboutDesc: Open Settings to change any of these.
bot.autoApproveMixedOn_one: Allow everything is mixed: on for the Bot, not confirmed for {{count}} helper
bot.autoApproveMixedOn_other: Allow everything is mixed: on for the Bot, not confirmed for {{count}} helpers
bot.autoApproveMixedOff_one: Allow everything is mixed: off for the Bot, but {{count}} helper has not confirmed it and may still approve alone
bot.autoApproveMixedOff_other: Allow everything is mixed: off for the Bot, but {{count}} helpers have not confirmed it and may still approve alone
bot.autoApproveRefused_one: Allow everything is mixed: on for the Bot, but {{count}} helper's approval policy does not allow it
bot.autoApproveRefused_other: Allow everything is mixed: on for the Bot, but {{count}} helpers' approval policies do not allow it
autoapprove.confirmBody: This Bot's helpers will run commands and change files without asking you first, as you, including some actions normally kept for a person. Deny rules still win, and questions still wait for you. It takes effect on their next action.
autoapprove.unknown: Allow everything may have changed. Check before pressing it again.
newBot.autoOn: On: it runs commands and edits files without asking. Change it on the Bot's page.
newBot.autoOff: Off: it asks when a step needs you; your rules and hooks can let a step run without asking. Change it on the Bot's page.
bot.defaultHelp: The default Bot of a realm answers when something asks for a Bot without naming one. If you delete it, a new empty one is made the next time it is needed.
bot.gone: This Bot isn't here any more
bot.goneBody: It may have been deleted, or its computer stopped. Pick another Bot from the list.
bot.hostingBody: This Bot runs on {{computer}}. It starts its tasks there. With permission it can also use the other computers of its realm; you choose which under Settings, Guardrails and limits.
bot.needsUpdate: This computer's agent is too old for this action. Update it from Computers.
bot.pausedBody: It does nothing more on its own until you send it a message.
bot.pausedBodyCount: It used {{used}} of {{max}} actions on its own. It does nothing more on its own until you send it a message.
list.privacyTip: Privacy is on in @BotFather: in groups, the Bot sees only commands and replies to its own messages.
chan.chat.cantRead: The Bot can't read this group: privacy is on and it isn't an admin here. It sees only commands and replies to it.
bot.stopAt: Asks the reply the Bot was working on at {{time}} to stop, if it is still running. Tasks it started keep running; stop them under Work in progress.
bot.stopMoved: The Bot has moved on from the reply it was working on at {{time}}. Stop asks only that reply to stop, if it still runs; later replies keep going.
bot.stopBody: Its current reply stops. Tasks it started keep running; stop them under Work in progress.
bot.stopLater: The reply now running may have started after this opened, so it is not stopped from here. Close this and press Stop again.
bot.stopTitle: Stop what the Bot is doing?
bot.stopUnknown: The stop may have gone through
about.behaviour.auto: Allow everything: runs its steps without asking
gate.why: A check-in rule asks you before the Bot goes on.
start.elsewhere: Another page changed this computer and its result is not known. Only that page can stop tracking it.
start.dismissBody: The change may have gone through. If you stop tracking it, this page stops following it and lets you send another. Check first if you are not sure.
activity.title: Activity
activity.desc: The conversation as it is written, with what the Bot did in between.
activity.emptyBody: Messages to and from the Bot show here.
activity.olderFailed: Could not load older messages. Try again.
archive.title: Archive of {{name}}
archive.desc: Messages moved out of the conversation by Start over or Forget, newest last. Read only.
archive.emptyBody: Start over and Forget move the conversation here.
log.place.elsewhere: session on {{session}}, runs on another computer
work.title: Work in progress
work.desc: The tasks the Bot opened, what each is doing, and what it waits on.
work.emptyBody: When the Bot starts a task it shows here.
work.unknown: The stop may have gone through
work.unknownBody: The stop may have gone through. Check before trying again.
work.finishedError: Could not read the finished tasks.
link.title: Link and keys
link.desc: A public address people and programs can call, protected by keys.
link.noneBody: A link gives this Bot its own address that apps and people can call with a key. Nothing is public until you make a key.
link.nameOnly: It starts with {{name}}. The full address shows once it exists.
link.platformPreview: {{url}}, if Bot links are on here
link.door.unavailable: Links aren't available on this computer right now. Try again in a moment.
link.door.unsupported: This computer's agent can't give links yet. Update it from Computers.
link.unknownStatus: The status of this link isn't known to this version of the Hub.
keys.desc: Whoever holds a key can use this Bot through its link. Give each person or program its own.
keys.revokeAllBody: Everything that uses one of these keys stops working at once.
keys.revokeAllUndo: A revoked key cannot be brought back. You make new keys one by one.
keys.revokeAllMaybe: Revoking the keys may have gone through
keys.revokeAllMaybeBody: The answer was lost. Check again before pressing the button.
keys.emptyBody: The link refuses every call until you make a key.
keys.unknown: The key list couldn't be read, so it isn't shown. Refresh to try again.
keys.col.name: Key
keys.full: A link holds at most {{max}} keys. Revoke one to make another.
keys.notConfirmed: The key change may have gone through
key.revokeBody: Anything that uses it stops working at once. This can't be undone.
key.rotateBody: A new secret replaces the old one, which stops working at once. You'll see the new secret once.
keyForm.desc: A key lets one person or program call the link.
keyForm.name: Name
keyForm.nameHelp: Up to 32 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes or underscores.
keyForm.nameBad: Use 1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes or underscores, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
keyForm.nameTaken: This link already has a key with this name. Use another name.
keyForm.expiresHelp: Optional. A date you pick ends at the end of that day (UTC); leave it alone to keep the key's current expiry.
keyForm.expiresPast: Pick a day that hasn't passed yet.
keyForm.expiresHelpNew: Optional. Leave it empty and the key never expires; a date you pick ends at the end of that day (UTC).
keyForm.sec.accessHelp: Where the key may be used from, and until when.
keyForm.holderNoteHelp: Shown to whoever uses this key, as plain text. Leave empty for none.
keyForm.maybe: The key may have been made
keyForm.maybeBody: Don't make it again. Check the list; if it's there, rotate it to get a new secret.
keyForm.editMaybe: The change may have been saved
keyForm.editMaybeBody: Check the key in the list before you save again.
keyForm.locked: Too many wrong two-step codes. Wait a few minutes, then try again with the newest code.
keyForm.gone: This key isn't on the link any more. Close this and check the list of keys.
keyForm.unread: The link's keys aren't read yet, so this key can't be edited. Wait a moment, or close this and try again.
secret.title: Copy the key “{{name}}” now
secret.note: This is the only time you'll see it. Store it somewhere safe; if you lose it, rotate the key.
secret.closeAsk: Close? This will not be shown again.
keyShare.qrWarn: The code with the key holds the key itself. Show it only to the device that should use it; anyone who scans it can use this Bot.
keyShare.qrShow: Show the code with the key
keyShare.qrHide: Hide the code with the key
keyShare.qrLabel: QR code: the Bot's address with its key
keyShare.qrPlainLabel: QR code: the Bot's address, without the key
keyShare.qrHiddenLabel: QR code, hidden until you press Show
keyShare.qrTooLong: The address with the key is too long for a QR code. Copy the key instead.
keyShare.qrNoUrl: No QR code yet: the Bot has no address. Copy the key instead.
secret.unknown: The rotation may have gone through
secret.unknownBody: The rotation may have gone through, but the new secret didn't reach you. Check, then rotate again if needed.
link.any.noAddress: This link has no address yet. It gets one once Bot links are on here; check back later.
connect.desc: Examples that call this Bot through its link. They read your key from HOODY_BOT_KEY.
panic.title: Panic
panic.desc: If a key leaked or the Bot misbehaves, one press turns the link off and revokes every key.
panic.confirmTitle: Turn off the link and revoke every key?
panic.confirmBody: Everything that calls {{name}} through its link stops working at once. You can make new keys later.
giveLink.title: Give it a link
giveLink.desc: A public address for {{name}}. People and programs call it with a key.
giveLink.labelHelp: Leave empty to use the suggested one. 8 to 48 lowercase letters, digits or single dashes.
giveLink.corsHelp: CORS: lets a page on another website call the link from a browser.
giveLink.keyNext: Next: make a key once the link exists. Nothing is public until you make a key.
giveLink.corsWhy: When should I turn CORS off?
giveLink.corsWhyText: Servers and apps are not affected. Turn it off if only your own code on a server calls the link.
giveLink.maybe: The link may have been made
giveLink.maybeBody: Don't create it again. Check the state first.
giveLink.unread: The address isn't read yet, so a link can't be made. Wait a moment, or close this and try again.
label.err.bad_char: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes only.
label.err.bad_end: End with a letter or digit.
label.err.double_hyphen: Don't use two dashes in a row.
label.err.taken: This name is taken. Type another one.
label.err.reserved: This name is reserved. Type another one.
linkSet.title: Link settings
linkSet.desc: Browser access, limits and removing the link.
linkSet.why: What do CORS and the limits do?
linkSet.whyText: CORS only governs calls from a browser; servers and apps are not affected. Calls over a limit are refused until the minute passes or a call finishes.
linkSet.rangeBad: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
linkSet.deleteHelp: The address stops working and its keys are removed. The Bot stays.
linkSet.deleteBody: The address stops working at once and its keys are removed. The Bot stays.
ip.label: Allowed addresses
ip.help: IPv4 addresses or ranges, one per line or separated by commas (up to {{max}}). Empty means any address can use it.
ip.err.ipv6: {{entry}} is IPv6. Only IPv4 is supported.
ip.err.host_bits: {{entry}} isn't a whole range. Write its first address.
settings.title: Settings for {{name}}
settings.maybe: Your changes may have been saved
settings.maybeBody: Check the current state before saving again.
model.title: Model
model.desc: The model the Bot itself answers you with. Helpers it starts don't use it.
model.restartNote: Saved changes keep the current model until its conversation restarts.
model.why.unread: Checking models… Try again in a moment.
model.why.consent: We can't tell yet if {{model}} runs on {{computer}}. Use it anyway, or choose another model.
model.why.setup: {{model}} needs setup on {{computer}}. Choose it in the list above to set it up.
model.why.gone: {{model}} is no longer on {{computer}}. Choose another model.
model.why.ineligible: {{model}} can't be used for a Bot. Choose another model.
model.wait: Wait for the save to finish
model.saved.unknown: Saved. We can't tell yet if it runs on {{computer}}.
model.saved.inherit: Saved. It uses the agent's configured model.
behaviour.title: Behaviour
behaviour.desc: Its name, role and standing instructions.
behaviour.name: Name
behaviour.roleHelp: One line that says what it is for.
behaviour.instructionsHelp: How it should work and talk. Guardrails are separate.
behaviour.instr.control: Remove the control characters. Line breaks and tabs are fine.
behaviour.instr.invisible: Remove the invisible characters. Some joined emoji hold one.
behaviour.fix: Change the marked field to save.
behaviour.refusedInstructions: The instructions were refused. Change them and save again.
behaviour.yoloOn: On: its helpers run without asking you. Takes effect on their next action.
behaviour.yoloOff: Off: its helpers ask you when a step needs you; your rules and hooks can let a step run without asking.
behaviour.mcpHints: Tell connected apps what is waiting
behaviour.mcpHintsOn: On: each answer to an app connected by MCP ends with how many new messages and approvals wait for it.
behaviour.mcpHintsOff: Off: apps learn what waits only when they ask for the status.
guard.title: Guardrails and limits
guard.desc: Limits on the work this Bot and its new tasks may do. They aren't instructions to the Bot.
guard.needsUpdate: This computer's agent is too old to change guardrails from here. Update it from Computers.
guard.rulesTooLong: Too long: with the Bot's name, role and instructions these rules pass the size limit. Shorten them.
guard.rulesHelp: One rule per line. Tasks already running keep the limits they started with.
guard.mode.strict.help: Work that may break a rule is refused, and so is work that can't be checked.
guard.mode.lenient.help: Work that may break a rule is refused. If the check can't run, the work goes ahead.
guard.offBody: Tasks and messages go out without being checked against the rules.
guard.computersHelp: Turn it off to limit its tasks to the computers you list.
voice.title: Voice
voice.desc: Speaking to this Bot and hearing it answer.
voice.promptHelp: Words that help the listening model spell names and terms right. Not every model takes one: if the save is refused, clear it.
voice.why.not_configured: No model is set for this, and the agent's default voices are off. Choose your own models, or ask whoever runs the agent to turn the default voices on.
voice.why.wire_not_built: This model cannot be used here. Pick another model.
voice.why.unknown_model: The agent does not know this model. Pick another one.
voice.why.not_an_stt_model: This model cannot listen. Pick another listening model.
voice.why.not_a_tts_model: This model cannot speak. Pick another speaking model.
voice.why.provider_refused: This model is not available now. Pick another one.
voice.why.unavailable: This model is not available now. Pick another one.
voice.why.voice_not_found: This voice does not belong to the speaking model. Pick another voice.
voice.why.language_not_supported: The model does not take this language. Pick another language, or leave it empty.
voice.why.no_credentials: No key is set on this computer for this model's provider.
voice.why.other: The agent reported a problem with this model.
voice.unknown: We couldn't tell if voice works.
voice.unknownHelp: The check did not get an answer. Nothing is known to be wrong.
voice.needsUpdate: This computer's agent is too old to change the voice from here. Update it from Computers.
voice.unchecked: Voice has not been checked yet.
voice.checking: Checking, this takes a few seconds.
voice.checkFailed: Could not check right now. Try again in a moment.
voice.custom: Choose the models and voice myself
voice.customOn: These choices are this Bot's own.
voice.customOff: The Bot uses the default voices. Press Check it works to see if they are ready.
voice.modelsFailed: Could not load the speech models.
voice.listenHelp: Turns what you say into text.
voice.voiceFreeHelp: This model lists no voices. Type one of its voice names, or leave it empty.
voice.languageHelp: A code such as en, or auto. Empty: the model's own choice.
voice.languageBad: Use a code such as en or pt-br, or auto.
voice.speedHelp: 1 is normal speed. Empty: the model's normal speed.
voice.speakWakes: Read replies about finished tasks aloud
voice.speakWakesHelp: Off: the Bot speaks only when it answers something you said.
voice.speakGates: Say out loud when it needs your approval
voice.speakGatesHelp: In a voice conversation, it tells you when an approval or a question is waiting.
voice.refused.generic: The Bot did not take these voice settings. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.tts_model.unknown_model: The speaking model is not one the agent knows. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.tts_model.not_tts: That model cannot speak. Pick another speaking model. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.tts_model.provider_refused: The speaking model is not available now. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.stt_model.unknown_model: The listening model is not one the agent knows. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.stt_model.not_stt: That model cannot listen. Pick another listening model. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.stt_model.provider_refused: The listening model is not available now. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.voice: That voice does not belong to the speaking model. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.language: The models do not take that language. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.speed: The speaking model does not take that speed. Nothing was changed.
voice.refused.limits: The Bot's own daily voice limits are outside what this realm allows. They can't be changed on this page. Nothing was changed.
voice.offLoses.prompt: Saving with this off also removes the Bot's transcription prompt.
voice.offLoses.limits: Saving with this off also removes the Bot's own daily voice limits.
voice.offLoses.both: Saving with this off also removes the Bot's transcription prompt and its own daily voice limits.
voice.offLoses.speech: Speech output is off now (its daily limit is 0). Saving removes that limit, so the default limits apply.
voice.offLoses.listen: Spoken messages are off now (their daily limit is 0). Saving removes that limit, so the default limits apply.
voice.refused.stt_prompt: The listening model does not take a transcription prompt. Clear the prompt and save again. Nothing was changed.
advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.desc: Read-only for now. Change these with the Hoody agent.
conv.reset.title: Restart the conversation?
conv.reset.what: The Bot starts a new conversation. The messages move to its archive.
conv.forget.title: Clear the conversation?
conv.forget.what: The Bot forgets what was said. The messages move to its archive; its settings stay.
conv.purge.title: Delete the archive?
conv.purge.what: Everything archived until now is deleted for good. The current conversation stays.
danger.delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
danger.delete.what: The Bot, its conversation and its archive are deleted. Tasks it is running are stopped where possible.
danger.delete.whatLink: The Bot, its conversation and its archive are deleted. Its link stops working and its keys are removed. Running tasks are stopped where possible.
danger.delete.whatLinkMaybe: The Bot, its conversation and its archive are deleted, and its link and keys if it has one. Running tasks are stopped where possible.
danger.delete.BOT_LINK_UNREAD: Could not check whether this Bot has a link, so nothing was deleted. Try again.
danger.delete.BOT_LINK_OTHER: This Bot's name still has the link of an earlier Bot, so nothing was deleted. Remove that link under Link and keys first.
danger.delete.BOT_LINK_NO_ACCESS: This sign-in cannot see or remove a Bot's link, so nothing was deleted. Delete the Bot signed in with full access.
danger.delete.BOT_LINK_OWNER_ONLY: Only the project's owner can remove this Bot's link, so the Bot was not deleted. Ask the owner to delete it.
danger.delete.BOT_LINK_KEPT: The Bot's link could not be removed, so the Bot was not deleted. Try again.
danger.delete.BOT_LINK_GONE_BOT_KEPT: The Bot's link was removed, but the Bot itself was not deleted. Try again.

newBot.host.none: No computer is running in this realm. Start one, then come back.
newBot.host.notRunning: {{name}} is not running, so a Bot can't run on it. Choose another computer.
newBot.host.otherRealm: {{name}} serves another realm. Choose another computer.
newBot.model.help: The model that answers you. You can change it later in the Bot's Settings, under Model.
newBot.model.setup: {{model}} needs setup on {{computer}}. Press Change to set it up.
newBot.linkOn: On: it gets a web address and a key; its secret shows once, after Create.
newBot.instructionsHelp: For example: Reply in short sentences.
newBot.name: Name
newBot.name.bad_id: Use letters, digits, dashes or underscores.
newBot.name.taken: A Bot with this identifier already exists on this computer.
newBot.name.reserved: That identifier is reserved. Choose another name.
newBot.linkUnread: The link's address isn't read yet. Wait, or turn Public link off for now.

newBot.instr.invisible: Remove the invisible characters. Some joined emoji hold one.

apps.desc: Let people talk to this Bot from the chat apps they already use.
apps.glance.title: At a glance
chan.emptyBody: Connect one to answer people where they already chat.
chan.removeBody: The Bot stops answering there. The people and chats it knew are forgotten.
chan.codeCancelled: The code no longer works. Make a new one when you need it.
chan.pausedAll: All chat apps of this Bot are paused.

chan.addFlow.say: Nothing is sent until you press Connect.
chan.addFlow.optionsWhat: A name for this app in the Hub
chan.addFlow.optionsWhat.telegram: A name for this app in the Hub, and the bot's webhook
chan.addFlow.needToken: Paste the bot token to connect.

chan.person.userIdBad: That is not a valid user ID for this app.
chan.person.ownerNeedsPairing: The first owner pairs with an owner code. This app has no owner yet; once it has one, the owner can hand over to someone added here.

chan.person.ownerMoved: Ownership changed while you were editing. Check again.

chan.person.userIdHelp: The ID the chat app uses for them, not their @username.
chan.person.name: Name (optional)
chan.person.langHelp: Replies to this person are written in this language.
chan.person.ownerHelp: An app has one owner, who has every right. Making this person the owner replaces the current owner.

faq.whatIsBot.q: What is a Bot, and where does it run?
faq.whatIsBot.a: A Bot works for you on one of your computers: it starts tasks and asks you before risky steps. You can reach it from here, from its chat apps, or from any app, agent or program that speaks HTTP, including OpenAI, Anthropic and MCP clients. It runs on one computer and starts its tasks there. With permission it can also use the other computers of its realm; you choose which under Settings, Guardrails and limits.
faq.defaultBot.q: What is the default Bot of a realm?
faq.defaultBot.a: The default Bot of a realm answers when something asks for a Bot without naming one. If you delete it, a new empty one is made the next time it is needed.
faq.linkKeys.q: What is a link, and what do keys do?
faq.linkKeys.a: A link gives this Bot its own address that apps and people can call with a key. Nothing is public until you make a key. Whoever holds a key can use this Bot through its link, so give each person or program its own. A link holds at most 20 keys. Turn the link off to refuse every call without deleting anything. Copy one of the addresses it answers on into the tool you want to connect, or open the chat page or the skill file. Other ways to use Hoody from code: install.hoody.com for the command line and sdk.hoody.com for the SDK.
faq.corsLimits.q: What do Other websites (CORS) and the call limits mean?
faq.corsLimits.a: CORS decides whether a page on another website may call this link from a browser. Servers and apps are not affected. Turn it off if only your own code on a server calls the link. The call limits count calls per minute and calls at once, for each key and for all keys together. Calls above a limit are refused until the minute passes or a call finishes. A key takes 1 to 600 calls a minute and 1 to 16 at once; all keys together take 1 to 3000 a minute and 1 to 32 at once.
faq.autoApprove.q: What does Allow everything do, and what does mixed mean?
faq.autoApprove.a: With Allow everything on, the Bot's helpers run commands and change files without asking you first, as you. Deny rules still win, and questions still wait for you. It takes effect on their next action. With it off, its helpers ask you when a step needs you; your rules and hooks can let a step run without asking. Mixed means the Bot and its helpers differ: on for the Bot, but some helpers have not confirmed it yet or their approval policies do not allow it; or off for the Bot, but some helpers have not confirmed it and may still approve alone.
faq.chatOwner.q: Who becomes the owner of a chat app, and how do others join?
faq.chatOwner.a: The owner decides who may use the Bot in an app, and has every right. The first person who sends the owner code to the Bot becomes its owner; you invite everyone else from People afterwards. The code works once and stops working after the minutes the setup steps show. To add someone, create a one-time code: they send it to the Bot in a private message and are paired with the rights you pick. Making someone else the owner replaces the current owner.
faq.telegramPrivacy.q: What does the warning that privacy is on mean?
faq.telegramPrivacy.a: The warning shows on a chat app whose bot has privacy on in @BotFather. While privacy is on, the Bot sees only commands and replies to its messages in groups. Turn privacy off in @BotFather: send /setprivacy, pick the bot and choose Disable. Then remove the Bot from each group and add it again: the change applies only then. Making the Bot an admin of a group also lets it read that one group. After you turn privacy off, pause and resume the app in Settings; the warning goes away once the agent reads privacy off.
faq.groupChats.q: What does the Bot read in a group?
faq.groupChats.a: A group asks to join when you, or someone with the right to stop and steer work, sends the bind command in it. The app's Group chats setting then decides: Ignore group chats lets none join, Only listed group chats only listed ones, Group chats I approve waits for your approval, and Any group chat lets it answer there at once, as a guest. The bind command can also be turned off. With Mentions only on, it answers what the app passes on that is meant for it; some apps pass a reply or a command only with a mention, and while a bot's privacy is on in @BotFather only commands and replies reach it.
faq.models.q: Which model answers me, and which do the Bot's helpers use?
faq.models.a: The Bot's own model is the one it answers you with; helpers it starts don't use it. A change applies when the Bot's conversation next restarts. Helpers are what the Bot starts to do the work. A change to them applies to helpers started after you save; helpers already working keep what they run on, and the Bot learns of it with its next message. Hoody-model helpers run on the AI helper's model, set on the AI page; a helper whose agent names its own model runs on that one, and Routing can pick per task instead.
